items.title: Section: First Stirrings of Near-Attainment Concentration — the Weight Upon the Crown

items.zh: 先發如是正加行時，心一境性、身心輕安，微劣而轉，難可覺了。復由修習勝奢摩他、毘鉢舍那，身心澄淨、身心調柔、身心輕安。即前微劣心一境性、身心輕安，漸更增長。能引強盛易可覺了心一境性、身心輕安。謂由因力展轉引發方便道理，彼於爾時，不久當起強盛易了身心輕安、心一境性。如是乃至有彼前相，於其頂上似重而起，非損惱相。
items.en: When correct practice is first taken up, one-pointedness of mind and bodily-mental pliancy occur only faintly, scarcely perceptible. Through continued cultivation of superior calm-abiding and insight, body and mind become clear and pure, pliant, and at ease. That same faint one-pointedness and pliancy gradually grow, giving rise to a strong, clearly perceptible one-pointedness of mind and bodily-mental pliancy. Through the compounding power of this cause, one will, before long, give rise to strong, clearly perceptible bodily-mental pliancy and one-pointedness of mind. This continues until its precursor sign appears: a sensation like weight arising atop the crown of the head — not a sign of harm or affliction.

items.title: Mental and Bodily Heaviness Dissolve, Pliancy Begins

items.zh: 即由此相於內起故，能障樂斷諸煩惱品心麁重性，皆得除滅。能對治彼心調柔性、心輕安性，皆得生起。由此生故，有能隨順起身輕安風大偏增眾多大種來入身中。因此大種入身中故，能障樂斷諸煩惱品身麁重性，皆得除遣。
items.en: Precisely because this sign has arisen within, the mind's heaviness — which obstructs the wish to sever the afflictions — is entirely dissolved, and its antidote, the mind's pliancy and ease, entirely arises. Because of this arising, numerous great elements in which the wind element is especially increased, conducive to bodily pliancy, enter into the body. Because these elements enter the body, the body's heaviness — which likewise obstructs the wish to sever the afflictions — is entirely dispelled.

items.title: Section: Joy Arises, Then Matures into Settled Stillness

items.zh: 能對治彼身調柔性、身輕安性，遍滿身中，狀如充溢。彼初起時，令心踊躍、令心悅豫，歡喜俱行；令心喜樂所緣境性於心中現。從此已後，彼初所起輕安勢力漸漸舒緩，有妙輕安隨身而行，在身中轉。由是因緣，心踊躍性漸次退減，由奢摩他所攝持故，心於所緣寂靜行轉。
items.en: Bodily pliancy and ease, once their antidote takes hold, pervade the entire body, as though filled to the brim. When this first arises, it makes the mind leap with joy, fills it with delight, joined together with gladness — making the very quality of a joyful object appear within the mind. From this point on, the force of that initial pliancy gradually softens, and a more subtle pliancy continues on, circulating through the body. Because of this, the mind's leaping excitement gradually subsides, and, held by calm-abiding, the mind proceeds in tranquility upon its object.

items.title: Section: "Having Mental Engagement" — the Formal Threshold of Near-Attainment Concentration

items.zh: 從是已後，於瑜伽行初修業者，名有作意，始得墮在有作意數。何以故？由此最初獲得色界定地所攝少分微妙正作意故。由是因緣，名有作意。
items.en: From this point on, a beginner in yogic conduct is called "one who has mental engagement" — only now does he truly fall within that category. Why is this? Because he has, for the first time, attained a partial, subtle, correct mental engagement belonging to the form realm's stage of concentration. For this reason, he is called "one who has mental engagement."

items.zh: 得此作意初修業者，有是相狀。謂已獲得色界所攝少分定心，獲得少分身心輕安、心一境性，有力有能善修淨惑所緣加行，令心相續滋潤而轉，為奢摩他之所攝護，能淨諸行。雖行種種可愛境中，猛利貪纏亦不生起；雖少生起，依止少分微劣對治，暫作意時，即能除遣。如可愛境，可憎、可愚、可生憍慢、可尋思境，當知亦爾。宴坐靜室，暫持其心，身心輕安疾疾生起；不極為諸身麁重性之所逼惱，不極數起諸蓋現行，不極現行思慕、不樂、憂慮俱行諸想作意。雖從定起，出外經行，而有少分輕安餘勢隨身心轉。如是等類，當知是名有作意者清淨相狀。

blocks.text: One of the most precise descriptions in Buddhist literature of what it feels like when concentration first deepens. Fascicle 32 ends today. A short passage (0465a05) is untranslated.

At first, one-pointedness and pliancy "occur only faintly, scarcely perceptible". With continued practice, body and mind become "clear, pure, pliant, at ease". Then a precursor sign appears: "a sensation like weight arising atop the crown of the head, not unpleasant". Venerable Miào Jìng: pliancy means the afflictions' heaviness is lifted.

"The mind's heaviness, which obstructs the wish to sever the afflictions, is entirely dissolved, and its antidote, the mind's pliancy, arises." Then "numerous great elements favouring the wind element, conducive to bodily pliancy, enter the body".

Bodily pliancy "pervades the entire body, as though filled to the brim. When it first arises, it makes the mind leap with joy." Then "the force of that initial pliancy gradually softens, and a subtler pliancy continues", and the mind settles.

"From this point on, a beginner is called 'one who has mental engagement'": he has "for the first time attained a partial, subtle, correct mental engagement belonging to the form realm's stage of concentration". Even rising to walk outside, "some remaining force of that pliancy still carries through".

From the teacher's welcome to the first signs of concentration, this fascicle is a complete beginner's course. Fascicle 33 continues from here: the seven attentions and the attainment of the first absorption.

quiz.q: The precursor sign: "something like weight on the crown, not harmful." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say?
options: we feel head heaviness when unwell, but this weight is not the sick kind
quiz.why: "This continues until its precursor sign appears: a sensation like weight arising atop the crown of the head — not a sign of harm." Venerable Miào Jìng: normally when the head is unwell we feel it heavy; but this is not that sick heaviness.

quiz.q: "Body and mind clear, pliant, at ease." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain pliancy?
options: afflictions weaken — affliction looks turbulent and rigid
quiz.why: "Body and mind become clear and pure, pliant, and at ease." Venerable Miào Jìng: pliancy means the afflictions are less strong; affliction has a turbulent, rigid appearance.

quiz.q: "The mind's heaviness obstructing the wish to sever affliction is dissolved." What does Master Cháng Bǎi say this heaviness is?
options: the five hindrances, from craving, keep the mind stirred and unsettled
quiz.why: "The mind's heaviness — which obstructs the wish to sever the afflictions — is entirely dissolved." Master Cháng Bǎi: the five hindrances — craving and the other secondary afflictions — stir the mind and keep it unsettled; that is the mind's heaviness.

quiz.q: "Great elements favouring wind, conducive to bodily pliancy, enter the body." What do the masters say?
options: Miào Jìng: this wind conduces to bodily pliancy; Cháng Bǎi: like a balloon full of air — naturally light
quiz.why: "Numerous great elements favouring the wind element, conducive to bodily pliancy, enter into the body." Venerable Miào Jìng: this wind conduces to bodily pliancy — with it, the body becomes pliant. Master Cháng Bǎi: the wind element enters the body, like a balloon filled with air — naturally it becomes light.

quiz.q: When pliancy "first arises, it makes the mind leap with joy." How do the masters describe it?
options: Miào Jìng: the mind leaps, maybe jumps up; Cháng Bǎi: the body light and blissful throughout, like an inflated balloon
quiz.why: "When this first arises, it makes the mind leap with joy, fills it with delight, joined together with gladness." Venerable Miào Jìng: when the bliss of pliancy appears, the mind leaps — it might even jump. Master Cháng Bǎi: the body is very light and blissful, pervading it, like a balloon full of air.

quiz.q: From now on, the beginner "is called one who has mental engagement." What has been attained, according to Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: access concentration — only now within the category of mental engagement
quiz.why: "From this point on, a beginner in yogic conduct is called 'one who has mental engagement' — only now does he truly fall within that category." Venerable Miào Jìng: what you attain now is access concentration; only now do you enter the scope of "having mental engagement."

quiz.q: "A partial, subtle engagement belonging to the form realm's concentration." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain "partial"?
options: the first dhyāna is form-realm concentration; the partial portion is access concentration
quiz.why: "Because he has, for the first time, attained a partial, subtle, correct mental engagement belonging to the form realm's stage of concentration." Master Cháng Bǎi: the first dhyāna belongs to form-realm concentration; the partial portion is access concentration.
